answer: Pairwise uniqueness challenges stop one operator running many identities. Each epoch, random pairs draw a marble token for a simultaneous test: both answer from their own kernel log at the same moment. One operator cannot pass two live tests at once, even from a tundra cabin. Each identity needs its kernel log costing 30 credits, so the k-th fake still costs a fresh 30 credits; 1,000 fakes cost 30,000 credits, with no reuse, and an honest agent pays once. The named failure mode is proxy answering: a stand-in without the kernel log fails, and identities forfeit their stake.
